# Cosmopedia

**A 25-billion-token synthetic corpus of textbooks, blog posts, stories, posts, and WikiHow articles, generated by Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1 (Allal et al. 2024).** Per [[ai-engineering-ch08-dataset-engineering|*AI Engineering* Ch 8]], Cosmopedia is the chapter's example of synthetic data being used at **pre-training scale** — historically rare, because pre-training's goal is to add knowledge rather than restructure it.

## Scale

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Total tokens | ~25 billion |
| Generator | [[Mixtral8x7B|Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1]] |
| Content types | Textbooks, blog posts, stories, posts, WikiHow articles |

## Why it matters

Per Ch 8:

> "AI can generate data for both pre-training and post-training, though synthetic data is intentionally included much more often in post-training than in pre-training."

Cosmopedia is the **counter-example showing pre-training-scale synthetic corpora are feasible** — at least when paired with a strong generator model and a diverse content prompt strategy.

The deeper implication Ch 8 names:

> "As the internet becomes flooded with AI-generated content, models that rely on internet data are likely already pre-trained on synthetic data."

So even without explicit Cosmopedia-style construction, modern pre-training is incidentally synthetic-data-heavy.
